title: Canonical restriction of strict derived towers to arithmetic subsequences
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site, let $\mathcal O$ be a sheaf of commutative rings, and let $\mathcal A=\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O)$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Put $J=\mathbf N_{\geq1}^{\mathrm{op}}$ and $\operatorname{Tow}(\mathcal A)=\operatorname{Fun}(J,\mathcal A)$ with componentwise exactness. Use its ordinary unbounded derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] and the total right derived inverse-limit functor and natural Roos model of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit]. For $e\geq1$, let $r_e$ be exact restriction of a strict tower along $n\mapsto en$, so $(r_eX)_n=X_{en}$ with transition $s_{en,e(n+1)}$. Here $s_{i,j}:X_j\to X_i$ is the composite transition and $s_{i,i}=1$.

The canonical restriction comparison is a natural isomorphism
$$\rho_{e,X}:R\!\lim_J X\xrightarrow{\sim}R\!\lim_J r_eX.$$
In the functorial Roos models, its map on the source products is coordinate selection $(x_i)_i\mapsto(x_{en})_n$, and its map on the target products is the finite-block map
$$(y_i)_i\longmapsto\left(\sum_{i=en}^{e(n+1)-1}s_{en,i}y_i\right)_n.$$
These formulas are interpreted as maps of derived products, computed on simultaneous strict-tower resolutions; the cone map is the induced cochain cone map, rather than a separately chosen triangulated completion of a square. It satisfies $p_n\rho_{e,X}=p_{en}$ for the derived-limit projections to $X_{en}$, and is natural for every morphism in $D(\operatorname{Tow}(\mathcal A))$. For $e=1$ it is the identity. If a strict cone $\Delta K\to X$ of complexes induces the quotient-cone map $u:K\to R\!\lim X$, the cone obtained by retaining the levels $en$ induces $u_e$ with $\rho_{e,X}u=u_e$. Thus strict squares, their induced total-limit maps, and their specified cone units commute with this restriction. No exactness of countable products of sheaves is assumed.

source.place: Tag 0H9K, lemma-pro-isomorphism-iso-Rlim, proof and its two product maps; Tag 0H9L, lemma-pro-isomorphism-Rlim, supplies only a noncanonical triangulated isomorphism. The canonical strict-tower restriction and cone-unit assertion is an agent-extracted ringed-site refinement using the functorial Roos model.

proof.text: Write $c(i)=\lceil i/e\rceil$ for the least positive integer with $i\leq ec(i)$. For a tower $T$, set $(L_eT)_i=T_{c(i)}$, with transitions those of $T$ (identities when $c(i)=c(i+1)$). This is additive and exact by levelwise exactness [lem-weil-tower-category-levelwise-abelian]. It is left adjoint to $r_e$: a map $f:T\to r_eX$ gives $(L_eT)_i\to X_i$ equal to $s^X_{i,ec(i)}f_{c(i)}$, and the inverse sends $g:L_eT\to X$ to $g_{en}:T_n\to X_{en}$. The inverse identities follow from $c(en)=n$ and naturality of $g$ along $ec(i)\to i$; the same formulas show naturality in $T,X$. Thus this exact adjunction is established directly, including the initial block $1\leq i<e$.

source.place: Tag 0941 (lemma-derived-limit-is-ok), exact-left-adjoint method; explicit arithmetic-index adjunction by the agent

proof.text: Realize towers as module sheaves on the small site $\mathcal C\times\mathbf N_{\geq1}$, whose arrows $(U,i)\to(V,j)$ are arrows $U\to V$ for $i\leq j$ and whose coverings have fixed index. Its coefficient sheaf is $\mathcal O(U,i)=\mathcal O(U)$. The sheaf and module axioms at each index give exactly the objects and morphisms of $\operatorname{Tow}(\mathcal A)$. By [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist] choose a functorial resolution $X\to I$ that is K-injective as a tower complex and has injective tower objects in every cochain degree. Step 1 and [lem-weil-pbc-right-adjoint-preserves-kinjective] imply that $r_eI$ is K-injective. Restriction is exact, so $r_eX\to r_eI$ is a quasi-isomorphism. By [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit], $L=\lim_i I_i$ and $L_e=\lim_n I_{en}$ compute respectively $R\lim X$ and $R\lim r_eX$. We have therefore obtained simultaneous resolutions; no acyclicity of arbitrary products is being asserted.

The ordinary restriction map $\alpha:L\to L_e$ selects coordinates $en$. Its inverse $\beta$ sends a compatible family $(z_n)$ to $x_i=s_{i,ec(i)}z_{c(i)}$. To check compatibility, for $i\leq j$ put $a=c(i)\leq b=c(j)$; then $s_{i,j}x_j=s_{i,eb}z_b=s_{i,ea}s_{ea,eb}z_b=s_{i,ea}z_a=x_i$. Also $(\alpha\beta z)_n=z_n$, since $c(en)=n$, while $(\beta\alpha x)_i=s_{i,ec(i)}x_{ec(i)}=x_i$. These formulas define sheaf morphisms and commute with the cochain differential because every $s_{i,j}$ is a chain map. Hence $\alpha$ is a chain isomorphism, natural in strict maps of tower complexes. This is the ordinary limit restriction comparison whose total derived comparison we will identify in the Roos models.

source.place: Tag 0H9K (lemma-pro-isomorphism-iso-Rlim), restriction on compatible families; explicit inverse for the arithmetic subsequence

proof.text: Evaluation gives K-injective complexes $I_i$ by [lem-weil-tower-evaluation-kinjective]. Module-sheaf products exist sectionwise: coordinatewise restrictions and module actions give a sheaf because each coordinate of a matching family glues uniquely. Thus form the termwise product complexes $P=\prod_i I_i$ and $P_e=\prod_n I_{en}$. By [lem-pc-ringed-space-product-kinjective] they represent the products $\prod_i^D X_i$ and $\prod_n^D X_{en}$ in the derived category. Define $\delta=1-s$ and $\delta_e=1-s_e$, so $(\delta x)_i=x_i-s_{i,i+1}x_{i+1}$ and $(\delta_e z)_n=z_n-s_{en,e(n+1)}z_{n+1}$. Their termwise kernels are exactly $L$ and $L_e$.

source.place: Tag 0941 (lemma-derived-limit-is-ok), evaluated K-injectives and derived products; derived.tex Tag 0BK6 (lemma-product-K-injective)

proof.text: For an injective tower object $J$, let $T_n(F)$ equal $F$ at indices $i\leq n$ and zero otherwise, with identity nonzero transitions. Tower maps $T_n(F)\to J$ correspond to maps $F\to J_n$, by propagating along the transitions. The inclusion $T_n(F)\hookrightarrow T_{n+1}(F)$ is monic by [lem-weil-tower-category-levelwise-abelian]. Take $F=J_n$ and extend the map corresponding to $1_{J_n}$ across that inclusion using injectivity [def-sp-injective-resolutions]. Its component at $n+1$ is a section $\sigma_n:J_n\to J_{n+1}$ of the transition $q_n:J_{n+1}\to J_n$. For $J=I^r$, this gives such sections in every cochain degree $r$. The composite $\sigma_{e(n+1)-1}\cdots\sigma_{en}$ is a section of $J_{e(n+1)}\to J_{en}$ as well. These sections are only degreewise; they need not commute with differentials.

source.place: Tag 0941 (lemma-derived-limit-is-ok), injective transitions; module-linear splitting proved from the definition of injectivity

proof.text: In each degree, $\delta:P^r\to P^r$ is surjective on sections: for any $(y_i)$ put $x_1=0$ and $x_{i+1}=\sigma_i(x_i-y_i)$, giving $x_i-q_ix_{i+1}=y_i$. The same recursion with the block sections of Step 5 proves that $\delta_e$ is degreewise epimorphic. Apply [lem-weil-degreewise-epi-kernel-cocone-qis] to these two epimorphisms. It supplies the specified quasi-isomorphisms $\kappa:L\to H=\operatorname{Cone}(\delta)[-1]$ and $\kappa_e:L_e\to H_e=\operatorname{Cone}(\delta_e)[-1]$, each given by $x\mapsto(0,x)$ with the kernel inclusion in the second component. In particular these are the cochain Roos models for the two derived limits of Step 2, with differential $d_H(y,x)=(-dy-\delta x,dx)$ and the analogous formula for $H_e$. This identifies their first vertices canonically at the complex level.

source.place: Kernel-to-shifted-cone comparison in the proof of Tag 070M (lemma-difficulty-K-injectives), in its explicit signed form stated by the cited node; sites-cohomology.tex Tag 0941

proof.text:
Define chain maps $a,b:P\to P_e$ by $a(x)_n=x_{en}$ and $b(y)_n=\sum_{i=en}^{e(n+1)-1}s_{en,i}y_i$. They are morphisms by the product universal property [def-weil-category-product], since each component uses finitely many summands. The square is strictly commutative: in coordinate $n$,
$$ (b\delta x)_n=\sum_{i=en}^{e(n+1)-1}(s_{en,i}x_i-s_{en,i+1}x_{i+1})=x_{en}-s_{en,e(n+1)}x_{e(n+1)}=(\delta_e ax)_n.$$
Consequently the induced shifted-cone map is the specified chain map $c:H\to H_e$, $c(y,x)=(by,ax)$: the differentials satisfy $d_{H_e}c(y,x)=(-bdy-\delta_e ax,adx)=c(-dy-\delta x,dx)$. This uses the actual cone differential [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], rather than any completion of a triangulated square. By Step 4 these are precisely the asserted maps on the derived products.

source.place: Tag 0H9K (lemma-pro-isomorphism-iso-Rlim), proof, the maps varphi-prime and varphi-double-prime with m_n=en and varphi_n=identity

proof.text: The kernel inclusions and the two cone maps satisfy $c\kappa=\kappa_e\alpha$ strictly, since both send $x\in L$ to $(0,(x_{en})_n)$. In the derived category the quasi-isomorphisms $\kappa,\kappa_e$ are invertible [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], so $Q(c)=Q(\kappa_e)Q(\alpha)Q(\kappa)^{-1}$. It follows from the explicit inverse $\beta$ in Step 3 that $Q(c)$ is an isomorphism. Under the simultaneous-resolution identifications this is exactly the total derived restriction comparison $\rho_{e,X}$. The projection $H\to I_i$ is $(y,x)\mapsto x_i$, so the equation for the selected coordinate gives $p_n\rho_{e,X}=p_{en}$ in $D(\mathcal A)$.

source.place: Localization at quasi-isomorphisms and the signed cone model; sites-cohomology.tex Tags 0940 and 0941, with the explicit comparison of Steps 3 and 7

proof.text: For a chain map of resolved towers $f:I\to I'$, write $F=\prod_i f_i$ and $F_e=\prod_n f_{en}$. Strict transition compatibility gives $a'F=F_ea$ and $b'F=F_eb$, since each term satisfies $s'_{en,i}f_i=f_{en}s_{en,i}$. Thus $c$ is natural for these chain maps. By [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived], every morphism in $D(\operatorname{Tow}(\mathcal A))$ is represented by a unique homotopy class of chain maps between the K-injective tower representatives. Termwise inverse limit and restriction carry a tower homotopy to a homotopy, by applying them to $f-g=dh+hd$. Hence $\alpha$ descends to those homotopy classes, and Step 8 identifies its descended map with $Q(c)$. A change of K-injective representative is a homotopy equivalence by the same cited node, so the construction is independent of the resolutions under their canonical derived identifications. This proves naturality for every derived morphism. For $e=1$, both $a$ and $b$ are identities (each block has one summand), and so are $\alpha$ and $c$.

source.place: Tag 070I (lemma-K-injective), Hom in the homotopy and derived categories and homotopy equivalences; strict product calculations of more-algebra.tex Tag 0H9K

proof.text: Let $h:\Delta K\to X$ be the specified strict cone. After $X\to I$ write its components as $h_i:K\to I_i$. The compatible family $t=(h_i)_i:K\to P$ satisfies $\delta t=0$. Its specified Roos map is $U:K\to H$, $U=(0,t)$; equivalently it is $\kappa$ composed with the unique map $K\to L$ given by that compatible family. For the restricted cone it is $U_e=(0,(h_{en})_n)$. The cochain formula gives $cU=(0,at)=U_e$, and localization gives $\rho_{e,X}u=u_e$. For any strict square of tower maps, the two composites commute before localization; applying termwise limits gives its total-limit square. Step 9 says each edge commutes with $\rho_e$, and the displayed equality says each specified cone unit does too. Thus the strict-square and unit assertions follow as equalities of the specified maps. Only products of evaluated K-injectives and the degreewise splitting in Step 5 have been used, never exactness of arbitrary countable products.

split_report.summary: Ten steps give the exact expansion adjunction, simultaneous K-injective tower representatives, the explicit inverse to restriction on compatible families, derived products, degreewise split transitions, canonical kernel-to-cone comparisons, telescoping block maps, their identification with total derived restriction, derived naturality, and the strict-cone-unit identity.
